claims.statement: --temporary-checkout on knowledge-build, knowledge-orient, knowledge-check-rules and knowledge-audit reads the named commit from a temporary detached git worktree outside the checkout, then removes it, so a dirty active checkout (for example an untracked session receipt) or another local commit needs no hand-made clean clone. The flag is opt-in and the clean-source check is unchanged rather than exempting untracked files or reading dirty bytes. Hooks and configured external filters are disabled, and a commit that assigns a filter to a tracked path is refused. Orient, check-rules and audit report the unread active checkout in source_checkout and active_checkout.

claims.statement: Deferred alternative: read committed bytes from Git objects instead of checking the commit out, for index building (including the first call of workspace-query) and for orient, check-rules and audit. It would remove the checkout cost, roughly 10 s of a 15 to 20 s first call on the development host. The builder reads and fingerprints files from a checkout, and its tracked-file, symlink and filter checks assume one; source fingerprints are taken from checked-out bytes, which Git can convert (line endings, filters), so an object reader would be a second byte path that has to agree with every index already built.

claims.statement: A separate clone is not a neutral clean checkout for knowledge-audit. Source fingerprints are taken from checked-out bytes, after any line-ending conversion, so in a clone made under another core.autocrlf setting cited text files read as changed. A temporary worktree of the same repository uses that repository's configuration and checks out the same bytes as its ordinary checkout; the flag does not make differently configured clones agree.

attributes.composition: Integrated on 2026-11-10 with decision:verification-relevance-for-unowned-files. On a file no component owns, a verification claim that names the file by exact path is returned in verification_refs, and the records linked from verified components are returned in their categories, so none of them is listed as a candidate; the capability route starts from owning components only and adds nothing there. Candidates exclude every record a category holds, including records the category cut at its limit, which are counted only in that category's omission total. The two routes match citations differently: the verification route needs the exact file: reference, while the citation route also accepts a line or fragment suffix, so a verification claim that cites the file with a suffix is listed as a candidate
